quizzes.stem: A policy allows bedrock:* on * for an application's role. A reviewer asks for least privilege. Which rewrite fits?

options.a: Keep the policy as written and add a condition that requires SSL
options.b: Keep the wildcard action but name the single model's ARN in the resource
options.c: Replace the wildcard with a deny statement for every other model
options.d: List the one invoke action and name the single model's ARN

explanation.d: The page says to "grant only the permissions required to perform a task", by "defining the actions that can be taken on specific resources".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a wildcard action still grants more than "the permissions required to perform a task".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "By default, users and roles don't have permission to create or modify Amazon Bedrock resources", so a policy should add what is needed and not rely on denies.
explanation.a: Ruled out because conditions are a refinement on top of a narrow policy: "Both come after the basics: the right action on the right resource".

quizzes.stem: A service account holds a custom role with only aiplatform.endpoints.predict on a Claude endpoint. A script running as that account tries to change how the endpoint is deployed. What should the team expect?

options.a: It is refused, since the grant covers calling the model and no more
options.b: It goes through, since a role on an endpoint covers all of it
options.c: It goes through, since the account sits in the endpoint's project
options.d: It is refused, since a service account may never change an endpoint

explanation.a: The page says the predict role "grants the service account the ability to call the endpoint for predictions", and nothing beyond that.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the same grant comes "but not the ability of controlling the endpoint".
explanation.c: Ruled out because membership grants nothing by itself: "You grant access by assigning IAM roles to principals."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the kind of caller sets no limit of its own: "what it may do comes from the role it holds", so the missing permission is the reason.

quizzes.stem: A team adds the deploy permission to its invoker role just in case. How should a reviewer judge the change?

options.a: Remove it, since it replaces predict and the calls to Claude will fail
options.b: Accept it, since the predefined user role carries the same permission
options.c: Remove it, since the account could export other models in the project
options.d: Accept it, since a deploy grant only adds serving capacity to the endpoint

explanation.c: The page warns that the deploy permission "might allow a user to export other deployed or deployable models from the project".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a predefined role is no model to copy: "Predefined roles often contain more permissions than you need."
explanation.a: Ruled out because custom "roles hold exactly the permissions you list", so predict stays beside deploy.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page concludes "so an invoker role should not carry it".

quizzes.stem: A project must keep Claude traffic in the EU and use Sonnet 5.5. Which Vertex endpoint setting fits?

options.a: The global value, since its dynamic routing gives the most availability
options.b: The European multi-area value, since named places serve older names only
options.c: A specific region such as europe-west4, since it is the strictest choice
options.d: Any of the three, since the project's location decides where data stays

explanation.b: The page says a specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only and that the EU needs "the `eu` multi-region endpoint or a `europe-` region", so Sonnet 5.5 takes the multi-region value.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Global endpoints: Dynamic routing for maximum availability" promises availability only, while residency comes with the multi-region kind, "for data residency with high availability".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The endpoint decides where a request may be processed."

quizzes.stem: A team asks AWS for 8 million input tokens per minute on Bedrock. What do the docs say about getting it?

options.a: It needs only a self-service request, since it is above the default
options.b: It is within the default, so nothing more is needed
options.c: AWS alone decides, since the quota is a Bedrock matter only
options.d: It is above the self-service ceiling, so Anthropic must approve it

explanation.d: The page says "You can request up to 5 million input TPM and 500,000 output TPM without additional Anthropic approval", and 8 million is above it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." and 8 million is far above that.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the approval named is "without additional Anthropic approval", so Anthropic is part of the decision.
explanation.a: Ruled out because self-service stops at the ceiling, not at the default: "Above those figures, Anthropic has to approve."

quizzes.stem: A Google Cloud project using Claude receives an abuse report three weeks after the activity, and the team finds nothing to inspect. What should have been in place?

options.a: Anthropic retaining the project's prompts for the customer to review
options.b: Logs of both prompts and replies, retained for a month or longer
options.c: Logs of the prompts alone, since abuse shows in what people ask
options.d: Request logs rotated weekly, since abuse surfaces within days

explanation.b: Activity from three weeks back can only be inspected if both sides of each exchange were logged and kept past that gap, and the page says to "Enable 30-day request-response logging".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Turning on this service does not give Google or Anthropic any access to your content."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the logging covers "prompt and completion activity", not prompts alone.
explanation.d: Ruled out because Anthropic "recommends retaining activity logs on at least a 30-day rolling basis", and a weekly rotation would have deleted the activity before the report arrived.

quizzes.stem: A reviewer finds a single star in the resource field of a policy statement. Which practice rule does it break?

options.a: The document must carry the current version string at the top
options.b: Each entry must be a model ARN in a documented region, without wildcards
options.c: No action may hold a wildcard, and each must be one of the invoke actions
options.d: The statements must allow, and none may use NotAction or NotResource

explanation.b: The rule is "Every resource is a model ARN with a region from the Bedrock region list, the `anthropic.` model id form, and no wildcard."
explanation.a: Ruled out because that rule concerns the version: "The policy has the version `2012-10-17`", which a star in a resource does not change.
explanation.c: Ruled out because that rule concerns the action field, "no wildcard anywhere in an action", and the star sits in the resource.
explanation.d: Ruled out because that rule concerns the effect and the negated fields, "only `Allow` statements, and no `NotAction` or `NotResource`", and a star in a resource is neither.

quizzes.stem: A reviewer sees the ready-made aiplatform user bundle attached to the calling service account. What does the practice require instead?

options.a: A custom role of the project whose only permission is predict
options.b: The same bundle plus a deny for the deploy permission
options.c: A basic Editor grant scoped to one endpoint of the project
options.d: An organization-level predefined bundle with fewer permissions

explanation.a: The rule is "The Vertex role is a custom role (its `id` starts with `projects/` or `organizations/`, not `roles/`) whose only permission is `aiplatform.endpoints.predict`."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the rule asks for a role "whose only permission is `aiplatform.endpoints.predict`", and adding a deny leaves the bundle's extra permissions in place.
explanation.c: Ruled out because basic roles "provide access control to your Agent Platform resources at the project level", which a custom role is meant to avoid.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the id "starts with `projects/` or `organizations/`, not `roles/`", and a predefined id starts with `roles/`.

quizzes.stem: A quota file asks for 4,000,000 input and 800,000 output tokens per minute with anthropic_approval false. What does the review do?

options.a: It fails the request, since the second figure is above 500,000
options.b: It fails the request, since 4,000,000 is above the 2,000,000 default
options.c: It passes the request, since the input figure is under 5,000,000
options.d: It passes the request, since output has no quota of its own stated

explanation.a: The rule is "Without Anthropic's approval a quota request is at most 5,000,000 input tokens and 500,000 output tokens per minute.", and 800,000 output is above it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the default is only the starting quota, and a team "can request up to 5 million input TPM" on its own.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the ceiling has two figures, and either one can fail: "Past 5 million input and 500,000 output tokens per minute, Anthropic has to approve."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the self-service figures include "500,000 output TPM without additional Anthropic approval".

quizzes.stem: A project with residency us asks for endpoint us and model anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5. What does the review say?

options.a: It passes, since the multi-region value keeps the data in the us
options.b: It passes, since the id takes the form the model ARNs use
options.c: It fails, since a Vertex id carries no prefix of that kind
options.d: It fails, since the us value serves one older model only

explanation.c: The rule is "A Vertex model id never carries the `anthropic.` prefix", and the id asked for has it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because that form belongs to the Bedrock side, and "The Vertex model id is the plain name, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, with no `anthropic.` prefix."
explanation.a: Ruled out because residency is met but the prefix is a Bedrock rule, "a region from the Bedrock region list, the `anthropic.` model id form", and fails on Vertex.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the multi-region kind serves the new model: "A project that must stay in the EU and use Sonnet 5.5 therefore uses the `eu` multi-region endpoint".
